info.title: qb model gateway (C4)
info.description: The model gateway of quota-balancer, `qb gateway`: one model turn per request on a route alias, streamed as NDJSON events. The gateway picks a login through qbd, holds and refreshes its credential, moves to another login before the client has seen any event, and reports what it observed to qbd. Invariants: thinking blocks of another vendor than the picked one are dropped; tool-call ids pass through unchanged; vendor identity headers and prompt prefixes are added by the gateway, never by the client. Decisions: docs/adr/0001-model-gateway.md; prose contract: docs/api.md.

x-transport.protocol: HTTP/1.1 over a SOCK_STREAM unix socket, one request per connection; the peer is identified by SO_PEERCRED and must be the gateway's own uid or a configured client uid (else 401)
x-transport.request: JSON body with `Content-Length`, at most `max_request_bytes` (413 above); chunked request bodies are rejected
x-transport.stream: `POST /v1/model/turn` answers `200` with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson`, one `StreamEvent` per line; the head goes out together with the first event; `GET /v1/model/batches/{batch_id}/results` answers `200` the same way with the vendor's results lines, and a vendor body that breaks ends without the last chunk
x-transport.error: a request rejected before the turn starts gets a non-200 status with `Error` as the JSON body; every admitted turn is a `200` stream ending with exactly one `stop` or `error` event

post.summary: Run one model turn on a route alias and stream its events.

200.description: Chunked NDJSON stream, one `StreamEvent` per line, ending with exactly one `stop` or `error`.

default.description: Rejected before the turn started: 400 invalid, 401 caller not allowed (`auth`), 411 no Content-Length, 413 head over 8 KiB or body over `max_request_bytes`, 429 turn or connection cap reached (`overloaded`, `retry_after`). 400, 411 and 413 are all class `bad_request`, not retryable. `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.
Rejected before any work started; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: The ladder steps the caller's ladder routes run on, with each candidate's vendor, API family, model, effort, tier and the state of the gateway's logins of its vendor within the logins of the queried route or, for a role, of the step's routes; no pick and no lease. Exactly one of `route` and `role`: a ladder route's step of its difficulty, or every step of a role that a ladder route the caller may use names. The roles are those qbd runs (`GET /v1/roles` of qbd), the states come from qbd's `GET /v1/state`. 400 `bad_request` for neither, both or another parameter and for a pin or chain route; 404 `bad_request` for an unknown route, a role no ladder route names, a role qbd does not run or a route's step it lacks; 503 `unavailable` when qbd cannot be read. On the unix socket every caller reads every route. On the loopback listener only a named `[[fronts.clients]]` token, within its `routes`: 403 `auth` for a route outside them or a role none of them names, before qbd is asked, and for the unnamed client token; 401 `auth` without a client token. Every error is an `Error` on both listeners.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: Alias of a ladder route; exclusive with `role`.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: A qbd role that ladder routes name; exclusive with `route`.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Stop a running turn this caller started; the answer comes once the turn ended, or after 5 s. 404 when none runs with that id, 403 when another caller started it, both class `bad_request`; the class `cancelled` appears only in the stopped turn's stream.

default.description: Rejected before any work started; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Read the gateway's config file again; only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller. A config that parses and validates as at startup and changes no restart-only field serves every later turn; turns already admitted finish on theirs. A refusal is 400 `bad_request` whose message names the file and the field or line, and the running config stays. The body is ignored.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: The spend and open message batch reserves of each login with a `spend_cap` in the current UTC calendar month, in config order; only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Set a capped login's spend count to zero and report its `spend` window to qbd, so the login runs again; only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller. 400 `bad_request` for a login without a `spend_cap`, 500 `unavailable` when the spend file cannot be written.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: The lines of the gateway's `audit_file`, oldest first: the first `limit` entries with `at` at or after `since`; lines that do not parse or are longer than 64 KiB are counted in `skipped`. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. 404 `bad_request` without `audit_file`, 400 `bad_request` for another query parameter, one given twice or a value out of range; a missing file answers no entries.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix time; entries with an earlier `at` are left out. Default 0.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: Sums of the gateway's usage ledger over the window from `from` up to `to`, one row per bucket and group, ordered by `start`, then `group`; reads `usage.file` and the rotated files stamped at or after `from`, a missing file counting as empty, and counts in `skipped` the lines that do not parse or are longer than 64 KiB. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. 404 `bad_request` without `[usage]`; 400 `bad_request` naming the parameter for an unknown parameter, one given twice, a missing `from` or an invalid value, and 400 `bad_request` when the answer would have more than 10000 rows.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Unix time; lines with an earlier `at` are left out.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Unix time after `from` and at most 400 days later; lines with `at` at or after it are left out. Default the time of the request.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: What the rows are grouped by; absent, every line is one group.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: The UTC period of the rows; absent, the whole window is one bucket.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Create an Anthropic Message Batch on a pin or ladder route: the gateway asks qbd one pick limited to the route's `api_key` logins of the `anthropic` API family (every such login of the config when the route lists none), stores a pending record for the caller's `idempotency_key`, sends the requests to the vendor with `model` set to the picked model, reports the vendor's answer to qbd and binds the batch to the login in `batches.file` before it answers. Callers as for `POST /v1/model/turn`; not served on the loopback listener; body up to `max_request_bytes`. 404 `bad_request` without `[batches]`; 400 `bad_request`, before any pick, for a body that does not validate, an unknown or chain route, or a route without an `api_key` Anthropic login, and for a request whose `params.max_tokens` is not a positive integer; on a login with a `spend_cap` the pending record reserves half of the sum over the requests of the `params` JSON bytes at the model's `[prices]` input price plus `max_tokens` at its output price per million, after the pick: 400 `bad_request` naming the missing `[prices."<model>"]` entry of the picked model, and 429 `quota_exhausted` with `resets_at` the month's end, nothing stored or sent and the lease released `error` with the login's `spend` window, when the month's spend plus the login's open reserves plus this reserve would pass the cap; the window goes to qbd after the record is written and after a refused or unsent create removes it; 409 `bad_request` for a key this caller used with another body, a key whose earlier submit has no known outcome, or a key whose submit is running; a repeat of the same body and key answers the stored batch's status without a create request. A pick that does not run answers as a turn would; the vendor's refusal answers its class; 502 `unavailable` when the request was not sent, or when its outcome is unknown, which keeps the key refused; 500 `unavailable` when `batches.file` cannot be written.

200.description: The batch the vendor created, or the one an earlier submit of the same body and key created.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: The vendor's status of a batch this gateway created, read through the login that created it, without a pick and also when the route changed since. Callers as for `POST /v1/model/turn`; not served on the loopback listener. 404 `bad_request` without `[batches]` or for an unknown `batch_id`; 403 `auth` for a batch of another caller, unless the caller is the gateway's own uid; 409 `unavailable` when the batch's login is no longer an `api_key` Anthropic login of the config; the vendor's refusal answers its class; 502 `unavailable` without an answer that holds a batch.

parameters.name: batch_id
parameters.description: The vendor's id of the batch, as `BatchStatus.batch_id`.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: The vendor's results of an ended batch this gateway created: the gateway reads the batch's status as `GET /v1/model/batches/{batch_id}` does, then sends `GET {base_url}/v1/messages/batches/{batch_id}/results` through the login that created it, never to the batch's `results_url`, without a pick. Callers as for `POST /v1/model/turn`; not served on the loopback listener. 404 `bad_request` without `[batches]` or for an unknown `batch_id`; 403 `auth` for a batch of another caller, unless the caller is the gateway's own uid; 409 `bad_request` naming the `processing_status` of a batch that has not ended, with no results request sent; 409 `unavailable` when the batch's login is no longer an `api_key` Anthropic login of the config; the vendor's refusal answers its class; 502 `unavailable` without an answer. The first read that reaches the end of the vendor's body settles the batch before the last chunk: each succeeded request costs its `usage` at half the `[prices]` entry of the batch's model (errored, canceled and expired requests nothing), the batch's cost is added once to the spend count of a login with a `spend_cap`, the store record is marked settled, which releases the submit's reserve also for a settlement at zero or without a price, the login's `spend` window is reported to qbd, and with `[usage]` one usage line with `batch: true`, `request_id` the batch id and the request's `custom_id` is appended per succeeded request. A model without a price gives lines without `usd` and adds no spend. A cut body, a caller that stops reading or a line that is not a result settles nothing; a settled batch's later reads change nothing. A read of an unsettled batch holds its settlement from before the results request; a concurrent read of the same batch settles nothing, and a failed spend count or store write lets the hold go for a later read.

parameters.name: batch_id
parameters.description: The vendor's id of the batch, as `BatchStatus.batch_id`.

200.description: Chunked NDJSON, the vendor's body passed through unchanged in its order, in chunks of at most 16 KiB. A vendor body that breaks after the head went out closes the connection without the last chunk.

schema.description: One line of the vendor's results.

result.description: `type` is `succeeded` with the Messages `message` and its `usage`, `errored` with `error`, `canceled` or `expired`.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Cancel a batch this gateway created: the gateway sends `POST {base_url}/v1/messages/batches/{batch_id}/cancel` through the login that created it, without a pick, and answers the vendor's status, usually `canceling`. The request has no body; any body is 400 `bad_request`. Callers as for `POST /v1/model/turn`; not served on the loopback listener. 404 `bad_request` without `[batches]` or for an unknown `batch_id`; 403 `auth` for a batch of another caller, unless the caller is the gateway's own uid; 409 `unavailable` when the batch's login is no longer an `api_key` Anthropic login of the config; the vendor's refusal, as for a batch that already ended, answers its class; 502 `unavailable` without an answer that holds a batch.

parameters.name: batch_id
parameters.description: The vendor's id of the batch, as `BatchStatus.batch_id`.

200.description: The batch's status after the cancel request.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Write 32 random bytes from the kernel, base64url-encoded, to the `token_file` of the `[[fronts.clients]]` entry `name` atomically with mode 0600; the next loopback connection accepts the new token, and the previous one stays accepted until `grace_until`, across reloads and restarts. The answer never holds the token. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. 404 `bad_request` for an unknown client, 409 `bad_request` for a client with `token_sha256`, 500 `unavailable` when a file cannot be written, the token file and the accepted tokens staying as they were.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The client's `name` as the config has it.

200.description: The client's token file holds a fresh token.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Write the body's key to the credential file of the `api_key` login `name` of the running config: the old file, when there is one, is copied to `<file>.bak-<unix s>` (`-<n>` appended when a backup of that second exists) with mode 0600, never over a file, and `{"type": "api_key", "key": "<key>"}` is written atomically with mode 0600; the login's next attempt sends the new key, without a reload or restart. Serialised with reloads, config edits and client token rotations. The answer, the log, the audit and the usage ledger never hold the key. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. Every request of a caller of the gateway is audited as `login_key`. 404 `bad_request` for an unknown login, 409 `bad_request` for a login that is not `api_key`, 400 `bad_request` for a body or key that does not validate, 413 `bad_request` for a body over 8 KiB, no message quoting the key or the body; 500 `unavailable` when a file cannot be read or written, the old file staying in force, except that a write which failed after replacing the file answers 500 `<file> was replaced but the write failed: <error>; the old file is kept as <backup>` and keeps the backup.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The login's `name` as the config has it.

200.description: The login's credential file holds the new key.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Start a PKCE (S256) sign-in of the `oauth_anthropic` or `chatgpt_oauth` login `name` of the running config, with no request body: the answer holds the vendor's authorize URL, what to paste back and the Unix time the sign-in expires, 600 s later. The verifier and the state come from the kernel's random source and stay in the gateway's memory only, zeroized when the sign-in ends; the state leaves the gateway only as a parameter of the URL. One pending sign-in per login: a new start replaces it. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. Every request of a caller of the gateway is audited as `login_oauth_start`; neither the log nor the audit holds the URL. 404 `bad_request` for an unknown login, 409 `bad_request` for an `api_key` login, 400 `bad_request` for a request with a body, 500 `unavailable` when the random source fails.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The login's `name` as the config has it.

200.description: The sign-in waits for the paste.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: Take what the operator pasted back after signing in at the URL of the login's pending sign-in, exchange its code at the login's `token_url`, else the vendor's token endpoints, and write the new tokens to the login's credential file: the old file, when there is one, is copied to `<file>.bak-<unix s>` (`-<n>` appended when a backup of that second exists) with mode 0600, never over a file, and the new file is written atomically with mode 0600; the login's next attempt sends the new token, without a reload or restart. The file write is serialised with reloads, config edits, client token rotations, key replacements and the login's token refreshes; the exchange is not. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. Every request of a caller of the gateway is audited as `login_oauth_code`. 404 `bad_request` for an unknown login; 409 `bad_request` for an `api_key` login, when no sign-in of the login is pending or it expired, or when the login's kind or credential file changed since the start; 400 `bad_request` for a body that does not validate, a paste without a code or with another state, the sign-in staying pending; 413 `bad_request` for a body over 8 KiB. Any exchange consumes the sign-in: 502 `auth` when the token endpoint refused the code, 502 `unavailable` when it could not be asked or its answer lacks a token or the account. 500 `unavailable` when a file cannot be read or written, as for `POST /v1/model/logins/{name}/key`. No answer, log line, audit line or usage line holds the code, the verifier, the state, a token or the account id.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The login's `name` as the config has it.

200.description: The login's credential file holds the new tokens.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: The `[[routes]]` items of the gateway's config file as it is on disk, in file order, which a reload has not necessarily taken, the `spend_cap` of every `api_key` login, and the file's hex SHA-256, also sent as the strong `ETag` `"<sha256>"`. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. 500 `unavailable` when the file cannot be read or does not validate.

200.description: The file's routes, spend caps and hash.

ETag.description: The file's hex SHA-256 in double quotes.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

put.summary: Edit the config file and reload it: `routes` replace its `[[routes]]` items, `spend_caps` set or remove the `spend_cap` of `api_key` logins, a body needs one of them or both. The new items are rendered as `[[routes]]` tables at the place of the first old item, the other old items are removed, and every byte outside the old items stays; comments inside them go. A file whose `routes` are an inline array, or with a table outside `routes` between an item and its `[[routes.chain]]`, is refused. An amount replaces the login's `spend_cap` value in place or adds a `spend_cap = <amount>` line after the login's last line, written so it parses back to the same number; `null` removes the `spend_cap` line; logins not named keep theirs; a login that is not a `[[logins]]` table of the file or not `api_key` is refused by name. The candidate file is validated as a reload validates the file. On success the old file is copied to `<config>.bak-<unix s>` (`-<n>` appended when a backup of that second exists) with mode 0600, the candidate is written atomically with mode 0600 and serves every later turn, and the spend view and qbd's `spend` windows follow the new caps. Serialised with reloads and client token rotations. Audited as `config_spend_caps` for a body of `spend_caps` only, else `config_routes`. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 for any other caller; not served on the loopback listener. 428 `bad_request` without `If-Match`, 412 `bad_request` when it is not the file's current hash, 400 `bad_request` for a body or candidate that does not validate (`routes refused: <file>: <field>: <reason>`, `spend_caps refused: …` for a body of `spend_caps` only, the line being the candidate's), 500 `unavailable` when a file cannot be read or written; on every refusal the file, its backups and the running config stay as they were, except that a write which failed after replacing the file answers 500 `<file> was replaced but not installed: <error>; the old file is kept as <backup>`, keeps the backup and installs nothing.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The config file's hex SHA-256 as `GET` answered it, with or without the double quotes of its `ETag`.

200.description: The file holds the edit and the gateway serves it.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

get.summary: qbd's roles as its files on disk hold them, with qbd's body and `ETag` unchanged. Forwarded to qbd's admin API on `qbd_socket` as the gateway itself (its uid or the bearer of `qbd_bearer_file`), so qbd serves it only when the gateway's `[[clients]]` entry has `admin = true`; docs/api.md, section "Admin `/v1/admin/*`", is qbd's contract. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 `auth` for any other caller before anything is sent to qbd; not served on the loopback listener. A non-200 answer of qbd becomes an `Error` with qbd's status and message, `auth` for qbd's 401 and 403 (whose message says the gateway's client needs `admin = true`), `overloaded` for 429, `unavailable` for 500 or an answer without an error body, `bad_request` otherwise; 503 `unavailable` when qbd cannot be reached.

ETag.description: qbd's `ETag`: the roles file's hex SHA-256 in double quotes.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

put.summary: Replace qbd's `roles_file` with the roles of the body and make them its running roles; the body and `If-Match` go to qbd unchanged, and qbd's body comes back unchanged. Audited as `admin_roles`, refusals included. Forwarded to qbd's admin API on `qbd_socket` as the gateway itself (its uid or the bearer of `qbd_bearer_file`), so qbd serves it only when the gateway's `[[clients]]` entry has `admin = true`; docs/api.md, section "Admin `/v1/admin/*`", is qbd's contract. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 `auth` for any other caller before anything is sent to qbd; not served on the loopback listener. A non-200 answer of qbd becomes an `Error` with qbd's status and message, `auth` for qbd's 401 and 403 (whose message says the gateway's client needs `admin = true`), `overloaded` for 429, `unavailable` for 500 or an answer without an error body, `bad_request` otherwise; 503 `unavailable` when qbd cannot be reached.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The roles file's hex SHA-256 as `GET` answered it, with or without the double quotes of its `ETag`; qbd answers 428 without it and 412 for another hash.

default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: qbd reads its config files again as on SIGHUP; qbd's body comes back unchanged. Audited as `admin_reload`, refusals included. Forwarded to qbd's admin API on `qbd_socket` as the gateway itself (its uid or the bearer of `qbd_bearer_file`), so qbd serves it only when the gateway's `[[clients]]` entry has `admin = true`; docs/api.md, section "Admin `/v1/admin/*`", is qbd's contract. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 `auth` for any other caller before anything is sent to qbd; not served on the loopback listener. default.description: Refused; `class` is authoritative, the status is informative.

post.summary: qbd clears the `auth_stale` or `auth_dead` mark of the logins named, or of every login with `all`, and journals each change; other marks stay; qbd's body comes back unchanged. Audited as `admin_logins_reset`, refusals included. Forwarded to qbd's admin API on `qbd_socket` as the gateway itself (its uid or the bearer of `qbd_bearer_file`), so qbd serves it only when the gateway's `[[clients]]` entry has `admin = true`; docs/api.md, section "Admin `/v1/admin/*`", is qbd's contract. Only the gateway's own uid, 403 `auth` for any other caller before anything is sent to qbd; not served on the loopback listener. A non-200 answer of qbd becomes an `Error` with qbd's status and message, `auth` for qbd's 401 and 403 (whose message says the gateway's client needs `admin = true`), `overloaded` for 429, `unavailable` for 500 or an answer without an error body, `bad_request` otherwise; 503 `unavailable` when qbd cannot be reached.

get.summary: Liveness and version, as qbd answers it.

TurnRequest.description: Body of `POST /v1/model/turn`: one model turn on a route alias. The client sends no vendor identity headers and no vendor prompt prefixes; qb adds them for the vendor it picks.

route.description: Route alias from the gateway config; it maps to a qbd role and ladder step, or to a pinned vendor and model.

system.description: System prompt of the client, without any vendor prefix.

max_tokens.description: Upper bound of output tokens for this turn.

session_key.description: Opaque session id: the `run_id` and `resume_of` of qbd's pick. qbd does not use `resume_of` yet, so turns of one session are not kept on one login; only a route's `logins` bound where a turn runs.

request_id.description: Client-chosen id of this turn, unique among running turns; `POST /v1/model/cancel` names it.

Effort.description: Reasoning effort; qb maps it to the vendor setting of the picked model.

CacheMode.description: Prompt cache policy; `auto` lets qb place cache breakpoints for the picked vendor, `auto_1h` the same with the vendor's one-hour lifetime where it has one (else as `auto`).

Role.description: Author of a message; tool results travel in `user` messages. A `system` message holds text blocks only: an instruction from that point of the conversation on, which an upstream that cannot place it there adds to the system prompt.

Block.description: One message block: `type` selects the variant and its fields. `text`: `text`. `image`: `media_type` and exactly one of `path` and `base64`. `tool_use`: `id`, `name`, `input`. `tool_result`: `id`, `content`, optional `is_error`. `thinking`: `vendor`, `opaque`, echoed back as received; qb drops `thinking` blocks of another vendor after a cross-vendor fallback.

path.description: Absolute path of a local image file (`image`). Part of the contract's shape; `qb gateway` reads no file a client names and answers 400 for it, so images go inline as `base64`.

base64.description: Standard base64 of the image bytes (`image`).

id.description: Tool-call id (`tool_use`, `tool_result`); qb keeps it stable across vendors.

is_error.description: The tool failed (`tool_result`); absent means false.

vendor.description: Vendor that produced the thinking (`thinking`): the qb vendor name the `route` event named.

opaque.description: Vendor thinking payload, passed back unchanged (`thinking`).

Tool.description: A tool the model may call.

name.description: Tool name, unique within the request.

description.description: What the tool does, for the model.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema of the tool arguments.

NativeTool.description: The tool as the client declared it in a vendor API, when it is not a plain function tool there. An upstream of that API sends `spec` as is; another follows `elsewhere`.

spec.description: The declaration as the client sent it.

elsewhere.description: `function`: offer it as a function tool of name, description and input_schema; `omit`: leave it out; `refuse`: fail the attempt with bad_request.

EventType.description: Kind of a stream event; `stop` and `error` are terminal.

StreamEvent.description: One NDJSON line of the turn stream: `type` and the one payload field of that variant (`route`: `route`, `text_delta`: `text`, `thinking`: `thinking`, `tool_call`: `tool_call`, `usage`: `usage`, `stop`: `reason`, `error`: `error`). A stream carries `route`, then any number of `text_delta`, `thinking`, `tool_call` and `usage` events, and ends with exactly one `stop` or `error`; a turn that fails before any vendor answered is one `error` without `route`. A stream that ends without a final event was cut by a transport failure.

text.description: Next piece of the answer text (`text_delta`).

RouteInfo.description: Where the gateway runs this turn; sent with the first content event of the attempt that answers.

vendor.description: qb vendor name from qbd's config.

login_label.description: Name of the login qbd picked; never a credential.

lease.description: qbd lease id of the attempt.

Thinking.description: A complete thinking block; the client stores it and echoes it back as a `thinking` block of the assistant message.

vendor.description: qb vendor name of the route that produced it.

opaque.description: Vendor thinking payload, passed back unchanged.

ToolCall.description: A complete tool call of the model; the client echoes it back as a `tool_use` block.

Usage.description: Token counts of the turn so far; a later `usage` event replaces an earlier one.

input.description: Input tokens neither read from nor written to the prompt cache; disjoint from `cache_read` and `cache_write`, so the whole input is their sum.

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

StopReason.description: Why the turn ended: `end` finished, `tool_use` waits for tool results, `max_tokens` hit the limit, `refusal` declined by the model.

ErrorClass.description: Failure class: `quota_exhausted` every candidate of the route waits for a reset or back-off (`resets_at` until when, retryable), `auth` a login or the caller was rejected, `unavailable` the vendor or qbd failed, `overloaded` back off (`retry_after`), `bad_request` the request is invalid, `context_too_long` the conversation does not fit the model, `cancelled` the turn was cancelled, `no_route` qbd has no candidate the route can ever run on.

Error.description: A failed turn: the payload of a terminal `error` event, and the body of every non-200 answer.

retryable.description: The same request may succeed if sent again later: after `retry_after` seconds, or at `resets_at`.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before a retry (`overloaded`).

resets_at.description: Unix time when the route's nearest candidate becomes usable again (`quota_exhausted`).

tried.description: Routes qb tried for this turn, in order.

Attempt.description: One login the turn tried and how it failed.

RouteState.description: State of a route alias from the logins it can run on in qbd's state: `ready` one of them is usable, `exhausted` all usable ones wait (`resets_at`), `unavailable` none is usable or qbd is unreachable. A chain route is `ready` when one step is, else `exhausted` when one step is, else `unavailable`. A login waits when it is `exhausted` or `rate_limited`, until its `dead_until`, or when it is `ok`, `unknown` or `auth_stale` with a window at `used` >= 1.0 and a reset, until the latest such reset. `degraded` is reserved and not sent.

RouteStatus.description: One route alias and the logins it can run on: this gateway's logins of the pinned vendor, of each step's vendor of a chain route, or every login of this gateway for a ladder route, within the route's `logins` when it has them.

vendor.description: Pinned vendor, or of a ready chain route the vendor of its first step with a ready login; absent for a ladder route.

model.description: Pinned model, or of a ready chain route the model of its first step with a ready login; absent for a ladder route.

resets_at.description: Earliest end of the waits of its logins, over every step of a chain route (`exhausted`): a `dead_until`, or the reset of a full window.

ApiFamily.description: The vendor API family a login speaks.

LadderCandidateState.description: A candidate of a ladder step and the state of the gateway's logins of its vendor.

api.description: API family of the gateway's first login, in config order, that qbd puts on the vendor, among the logins the state is taken over; absent when there is none.

effort.description: Reasoning effort; absent when the ladder has none.

state.description: `ready`, `exhausted` or `unavailable` by the rule of `GET /v1/model/routes` over the gateway's logins of the vendor: within the queried route's `logins` or, for a role, the union of the `logins` of the step's routes, a route without them adding every login.

resets_at.description: Earliest end of the waits of those logins (`exhausted`): a `dead_until`, or the reset of a full window.

LadderStepState.description: A ladder step of qbd's running role.

routes.description: Ladder route aliases the caller may use that name the step, sorted.

request_id.description: `request_id` of a running turn this caller started.

cancelled.description: Always true: the turn was stopped and ends with an `error` event of class `cancelled`.

ReloadAnswer.description: Answer of `POST /v1/model/reload`: the config now serving later turns.

routes.description: Route aliases of the new config.

LoginSpend.description: The spend of one login with a `spend_cap` in the current UTC calendar month.

spent_usd.description: USD counted this month: turns and settled message batches.

reserved_usd.description: USD the login's unsettled message batches submitted this month reserve, pending creates included. Absent in an answer of an older gateway.

cap_usd.description: The login's `spend_cap`; at or above it, `spent_usd` plus `reserved_usd`, the login is not called.

period_end.description: Unix time the month ends and the count starts again from zero.

logins.description: Every login of the config with a `spend_cap`, in config order.

login.description: The login whose count goes back to zero.

ClientRotateAnswer.description: Answer of `POST /v1/model/clients/{name}/rotate`. It never holds the token.

client.description: Name of the `[[fronts.clients]]` entry whose token was rotated.

token_sha256_prefix.description: The first 12 hex characters of the new token's SHA-256.

grace_until.description: Unix time until which the previous token stays accepted.

LoginKey.description: Request of `POST /v1/model/logins/{name}/key`: the login's new key.

key.description: The key: 1 to 4096 bytes of visible ASCII, no whitespace or control character.

LoginKeyAnswer.description: Answer of `POST /v1/model/logins/{name}/key`. It never holds the key.

login.description: Name of the `[[logins]]` entry whose key was replaced.

backup.description: Path of the copy of the credential file it replaced; `null` when the login had none.

key_sha256_prefix.description: The first 12 hex characters of the new key's SHA-256.

OauthPaste.description: What the operator pastes back: `code_state` for an `oauth_anthropic` login, the `code#state` the vendor's page shows; `redirect_url` for a `chatgpt_oauth` login, the full address of the localhost page the browser then fails to load.

login.description: Name of the `[[logins]]` entry signing in.

url.description: The vendor's authorize URL with the S256 challenge and the state.

expires_at.description: Unix time after which the sign-in takes no code.

pasted.description: What the operator pasted back, as `paste` of the start's answer says; surrounding whitespace is ignored.

LoginOauthSigned.description: Answer of `POST /v1/model/logins/{name}/oauth/code`. It never holds a code or a token.

login.description: Name of the `[[logins]]` entry signed in.

backup.description: Path of the copy of the credential file it replaced; `null` when the login had none.

AuditAction.description: An admin action: `reload` the config file read again, by `POST /v1/model/reload` or SIGHUP; `spend_reset` a login's spend count set to zero; `client_rotate` a fresh token written to a named loopback client's `token_file`; `config_routes` the config file's `[[routes]]` replaced, with any `spend_caps` set, by `PUT /v1/model/config/routes` and reloaded, also for a body that does not parse; `config_spend_caps` the `spend_cap`s of logins set or removed by a `PUT /v1/model/config/routes` of `spend_caps` only and reloaded; `login_key` a new key written to an `api_key` login's credential file by `POST /v1/model/logins/{name}/key`; `login_oauth_start` a sign-in of an OAuth login started by `POST /v1/model/logins/{name}/oauth/start`; `login_oauth_code` a sign-in's code exchanged and the new tokens written to the login's credential file by `POST /v1/model/logins/{name}/oauth/code`. `admin_roles` qbd's `roles_file` replaced by a `PUT /v1/admin/roles` forwarded to qbd; `admin_reload` qbd's config files read again by a `POST /v1/admin/reload` forwarded to qbd; `admin_logins_reset` auth marks of qbd's logins cleared by a `POST /v1/admin/logins/reset` forwarded to qbd.

AuditResult.description: `ok` the action answered 200; `refused` it was refused or failed, `reason` says why.

AuditEntry.description: One line of the gateway's `audit_file`. No field holds a token, key or credential content.

actor.description: `uid:<n>` for a unix socket caller, `signal` for a SIGHUP reload.

object.description: The config file of a reload or a routes edit, the login of a spend reset, a key replacement or a sign-in, the client of a rotation, `qbd_socket` of a request forwarded to qbd's admin API; absent when a refused request named none.

config_sha256_before.description: A reload or a routes edit: hex SHA-256 of the config file before the action. An `admin_roles` that went through: of qbd's roles file before it, the `If-Match` it sent.

config_sha256_after.description: A reload or a routes edit: hex SHA-256 of the config file after it; the same as before when it was refused. An `admin_roles` that went through: of qbd's roles file after it, the `sha256` qbd answered.

backup.description: A routes edit that went through, or that replaced the file but could not install it: path of the copy of the file it replaced; a key replacement or a sign-in's code that went through or failed after replacing the file: path of the copy of the credential file it replaced, absent when there was none. An `admin_roles` that went through: the `backup` qbd answered, absent when it wrote nothing.

token_sha256_prefix.description: A rotation that went through: the first 12 hex characters of the new token's SHA-256.

key_sha256_prefix.description: A key replacement that went through: the first 12 hex characters of the new key's SHA-256.

entries.description: The first `limit` entries at or after `since`, oldest first.

skipped.description: Lines of the file that do not parse as an entry or are longer than 64 KiB; they are left out.

UsageGroupBy.description: What usage rows are grouped by: the turn's `client`, the attempt's `login` or `model`, the turn's `route`, or each `tool` name of the attempt, under which an attempt counts once per name and not at all without tools, so the rows' sums overlap.

UsageBucket.description: The UTC period of usage rows: an `hour`, a `day` or a calendar `month`.

UsageRow.description: The sums of the usage lines of one bucket and group; sums saturate at the largest value of their type.

start.description: Start of the row's UTC bucket, which can lie before `from`; `from` without `bucket`.

group.description: The row's client, login, model, route or tool name; absent without `group_by`.

attempts.description: Lines counted, turn attempts and batch lines alike.

input.description: Input tokens neither read from nor written to the prompt cache; disjoint from `cache_read` and `cache_write`, so the whole input is their sum.

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

usd.description: Sum of the lines' `usd`, priced lines only.

rows.description: One row per bucket and group that holds a line, ordered by `start`, then `group`.

skipped.description: Lines of the files read that do not parse as a usage line or are longer than 64 KiB; they are left out.

route.description: Alias of a pin or ladder route.

idempotency_key.description: The caller's key of this submit; a repeat with the same body answers the batch it created, one with another body is 409.

custom_id.description: The caller's id of the request, unique in the batch.

params.description: Anthropic Messages parameters sent to the vendor as given, except that the gateway sets `model` to the picked model; a `model` or `stream` key, or a `max_tokens` that is missing or not a positive integer, is 400 `bad_request` naming the request's `custom_id`.

BatchProcessing.description: Where a batch is in its processing, as the vendor reports it.

BatchCounts.description: The requests of a batch by how far they got.

succeeded.description: Requests that ended with a message.

errored.description: Requests that ended with an error.

expired.description: Requests that did not run before the batch expired.

batch_id.description: The vendor's id of the batch.

route.description: Route alias the batch was submitted on.

login.description: Login that created the batch; every later request of the batch goes through it.

model.description: Model every request of the batch runs on.

created_at.description: Unix time the vendor created the batch.

ended_at.description: Unix time processing ended; absent before.

expires_at.description: Unix time the vendor expires the batch's unprocessed requests.

ConfigStep.description: One step of a chain route.

ConfigRoute.description: One `[[routes]]` item of the gateway config file, key for key (`config.md`). Integers take any 64-bit value: the config parser judges every value of a `PUT`.

chain.description: Pins a turn tries in order.

client_effort.description: Whose reasoning effort a turn sends: `use` (the client's, else the pick's) or `ignore` (the pick's only). Absent when the file has no key, which acts as `use`.

logins.description: Logins every pick of a turn on the route is limited to, each a `[[logins]]` name of this gateway config; absent for every login.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the config file.

spend_caps.description: Every `api_key` login by name with its `spend_cap` in USD, `null` for one without; logins of other kinds are not listed. Absent in an answer of an older gateway.

routes.description: The items that replace the file's `[[routes]]`, in file order; absent keeps them.

spend_caps.description: USD `spend_cap` of `api_key` logins by name, `null` to remove it; logins not named keep theirs. The candidate's validation refuses an amount that is not more than 0 or a cap without a top-level `spend_file`.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the config file written and now serving, or of the file left as it was.

backup.description: Path of the copy of the file it replaced; absent when the edit changed no byte and nothing was written.

AdminRoles.description: qbd's `GET /v1/admin/roles` answer: the roles of its files on disk.

source.description: `roles_file` when the config names one, else `config`.

file.description: Path of the file that holds the roles.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of that file's bytes; also the `ETag`.

RoleConfig.description: A role as qbd's config file declares it.

reserves.description: Reserves in file order; absent is none.

LadderStep.description: One ladder step of a role.

LadderCandidate.description: A vendor/model/effort combination of a ladder step.

effort.description: Reasoning effort; absent when the file has none.

cost_per_minute.description: Fraction of the vendor's shortest window one minute of work uses; absent when the file has none.

RoleReserve.description: Fraction of a window a role keeps free at a difficulty.

difficulty.description: Difficulty of a ladder step of the role.

AdminRolesPut.description: qbd's `PUT /v1/admin/roles` body: the roles that replace its `roles_file`, in the `GET` shape.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the roles file now on disk.

backup.description: Path of the copy of the file it replaced; absent when nothing was written.

AdminReloadAnswer.description: qbd's `POST /v1/admin/reload` answer: the counts of its new config.

AdminLoginsReset.description: qbd's `POST /v1/admin/logins/reset` request: exactly one of `logins` and `all`.

logins.description: Declared logins, by config name; an unknown one is 404 and clears nothing.
One entry per login, in declaration order with `all`, else in request order.

cleared.description: The login had an `auth_stale` or `auth_dead` mark, now cleared.
